verdict.rationale: dlt itself is a Python library without a built-in scheduler, but docs show it can be deployed to schedule-capable runners (Airflow, GitHub Actions, serverless) and dltHub's orchestration product explicitly says teams 'schedule, backfill, and chain their pipelines' and can 'Schedule lineage-aware pipeline runs with agents,' plus a one-command deploy that supports 'Schedule, refresh, backfill' workflows. This gives cron-style and manual-trigger control, but only via external orchestrators or the separate dltHub product rather than a native per-pipeline sub-hour scheduler in dlt core. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of sub-hour/cron granularity configuration UI, and direct confirmation of manual-trigger controls within dltHub's scheduling interface.
